# Colonial Partnership
The Company operates on the colony's land under a site lease. The colony and the Company need each other, and both sides know it. Handle the partnership as an asset. It's often the most valuable one on site.
All partnership business runs through the Contracts screen on the corporate console, the colonial administration console and the ambassador's console. Accounts settle every [bold]billing cycle of fifteen minutes[/bold].
## The colony's instruments - [bold]Site lease[/bold]: the colony sets the Company's rent, up to $1500 per cycle. Unpaid rent becomes arrears. - [bold]Research licence[/bold]: if it's revoked, all Company research at the site stops earning. - [bold]Tax break[/bold]: if it's revoked, Company supply orders pay sales tax plus a 50% levy. - [bold]Transit tariff[/bold]: charged on Company shipments.
These are the colony's to use, and it will use them. The Company's job is to make sure it doesn't want to.
## The Company's instruments - [bold]Development debt[/bold]: every colony begins in debt to the Company: $1500 at 15% interest, $1725 in all, from the start of each site's operation. - [bold]Loans[/bold]: the colonial ambassador may request financing of up to $10000. The interest rate is negotiated. Repayment is in three instalments, collected automatically each cycle. Each missed instalment charges the agreed interest again on what is still owed, and after three misses in a row the Company collects the instalment regardless, putting the borrower into debt to the Company. Generous terms buy goodwill. Strict terms buy leverage. - [bold]Work orders[/bold]: the Company may post up to three orders for colonial goods, paying 5–40% above market rate. Goods bought this way resell at a loss. A work order isn't a purchase: it's a gesture, offered to the colony when the Company wants the colony to feel generous.
## Contingency: Divestment When the partnership can't be saved, an executive of WYC6 or above may authorise divestment. The colony is given five minutes' notice, and once authorised, divestment cannot be called off. When the notice runs out: - Every outstanding loan is called in full, immediately, whether or not the colony can pay. - Work orders and the site lease are terminated. - The Company stops collecting the tariff. - Colonial trade costs 25% more and pays 25% less for the remainder of operations.
When divestment is authorised, a Company shuttle is dispatched at once. A Commercial Pilot and a security detail land to collect Company staff and assets. Have them ready at the landing zone before the notice runs out.
Divestment costs the Company dearly, and the executive who authorises it will be asked to justify it. It's a last resort. The threat of it is often more useful than its use.
